newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Q1 GDP data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Q1 GDP data.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts'
reactions to UK Q1 GDP data published at 0830 GMT.
* UK PRELIMINARY Q1 GDP +1.0%, +3.0% YY (vs forecast

PHILIP SHAW, UNION PLC ECONOMIST - "The figures demonstrate that economy remained buoyant during the first quarter. We had a slight acceleration in the pace of growth and they do provide another argument for a degree of overall policy restraint."

BANK OF AMERICA ECONOMIST JEREMY HAWKINS - "The UK GDP data were on the firmer side of expectations with a rise of 1.0 pct on the quarter and an increase of 3.0 pct on the year for both the headline rate and the underlying rate excluding oil production.

This was the highest year-on-year rate of growth since the first quarter of 1995. The service sector showed an increase of 1.2 pct on the quarter and 3.9 pct on the year - consistent with the evidence from the British Chamber of Commerce yesterday.
The figures may be a small negative for the interest rate markets and a small positive for the pound.
But are more likely to have a negligible impact. They are, however, consistent with the idea that interest rates will have to rise after the election."

SOCIETE GENERALE ECONOMIST TOM RAYNER - "What we will see now when we get the expenditure breakdown later in the month is that the consumption side is particularly strong because we already know retail sales in the first quarter have been pretty firm and it looks now that consumption and services as well are going to follow the same pattern.
So overall we are looking for a consumption led recovery with services being the main force."
ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND - "Slightly higher than market forecast UK first quarter preliminary GDP will be gilt and short sterling negative, sterling positive.
Services growth at 1.2 pct quarter-on-quarter 3.9 pct year-on-year - this confirms the boom the UK is currently experiencing in domestic demand.
Short sterling sell off may be limited. Since the strip is already pricing in 1.0 pct by the year end."
